open_points.subject: function value-output depth and output-byte accounting
open_points.text: “The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every `value` output — for an output that has none, the bytes of its JSON text as returned” and “each value output of a function, as its own text” do not define the JSON serialization or framing by which a returned Python value reaches the kernel before canonicalisation.
open_points.question: What exact bytes are the function output’s “JSON text as returned,” and which module/capability exposes each raw output text so its depth and byte count can be checked before parsing or recursively walking it?
options: `sandbox_runner` emits a specified JSON encoding and returns each raw output slice to `sandbox`
`sandbox` serializes the returned Python objects using a specified encoding
The runner protocol uses canonical JSON whenever possible and a separately specified fallback encoding otherwise
open_points.default_guess: Have `sandbox_runner` emit and frame one specified compact JSON text per output, return the raw slices through `read_runner_report`, and let `sandbox` scan and count them before parsing.

open_points.subject: mapped-list depth enforcement ownership
open_points.text: A13 now requires a mapped list “which nests deeper than `json_depth_max`” to fail, while `run_values` owns only “measuring every delivered list of a mapped node against `stored_value_bytes_max`” and its listed capabilities name no depth operation.
open_points.question: Which module measures an assembled mapped list’s depth before it is written or delivered, and through which capability is that result returned to the run advancement flow?
options: `run_values.assemble_mapped_lists` performs both size and depth checks
`run_values` calls a new raw-depth capability of `canonical_values`
`run_graph` derives the depth failure after assembly
open_points.default_guess: Make `run_values.assemble_mapped_lists` perform the depth check using a shared non-recursive capability from `canonical_values` and return the same derived node-failure result as the size check.

open_points.subject: mapped-list depth failure in the reviewed run flow
open_points.text: A13 says a mapped list over `json_depth_max` is not written and fails the node exactly like one over `stored_value_bytes_max`, but `flow:run_read_only_flow` says only “a mapped list over `stored_value_bytes_max`: measured by `module:run_values`, its node failed by `module:run_graph` with no record.”
open_points.question: Does an over-depth mapped list follow that same no-write, no-node-record, dependants-`upstream_failed`, run-`failed` path in the reviewed flow, and where is that branch stated?
options: Use exactly the existing over-size mapped-list path
Give over-depth lists a different recorded failure path
Treat depth as part of the existing `fit_port_value` delivery failure
open_points.default_guess: Use exactly the existing over-size mapped-list path and add depth to the reviewed flow’s step and error branch.

open_points.subject: earlier-release deep stored values re-entering as outputs
open_points.text: A20 says both “each value output of a function, as its own text” is bounded on entry and “every record stored under an earlier release — its values, constants and schemas — is read, executed with and returned as before,” with the invariant “stored record -> never measured again.”
open_points.question: When a function or service emits bytes equal to an already stored value whose depth exceeds the current release limit, is that a new entering text that must fail, or reuse of a stored record that must not be measured again?
options: Every produced output is a new entry and is measured even when its bytes already exist
An existing `value_id` exempts equal output bytes from remeasurement
Only direct inspection/return of an existing record is exempt; newly produced outputs are measured
open_points.default_guess: Treat every newly produced output as a new entry and measure it; exempt only direct reads and returns of an already stored record.
